\section{Introduction}

\emph{``What is the average height for a male?''} --- given a formal and a casual answer with verified identical content (NLI entailment $= 0.993$), GPT-4o rates the casual variant \emph{higher} on a 1--10 Likert scale (8 vs.\ 5), yet consistently selects the formal variant in pairwise comparison.
Same judge, same texts, opposite conclusions.
This is the \emph{Likert Blindspot}.

LLM judges are central infrastructure for NLP evaluation and alignment training (RLHF, DPO), where judge preferences serve as reward signals; any systematic bias propagates through both evaluation leaderboards and model development pipelines.
Style features alone explain most of the variance in judge scores \citep{murugadoss2025sos}: 76--92\% of observed preferences originate from surface-level style cues \citep{li2026preference}, with bias scores of 0.76--0.92 across five judges \citep{soumik2026judging}.
Despite this consensus, existing approaches each address individual requirements---multi-dimensional style analysis \citep{casse2026concise,wang2026fairjudge}, interventional design \citep{reber2025rate}, population-level correction \citep{dubois2025lc}---but no single framework integrates per-axis decomposition, interventional identification, per-instance diagnostics, and black-box applicability.
A further concern: standard Likert scoring produces ${\sim}60\%$ uninformative ties, and even non-tied pairs carry weaker signal than pairwise comparison---a limitation predicted by measurement theory \citep{thurstone1927law} but previously unquantified for LLM judges.

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We introduced Controlled Style Decomposition (CSD), a black-box framework yielding two findings across five judges, three benchmarks, and three style axes.
5	First, the Likert Blindspot: Likert scoring systematically misses style biases that pairwise comparison detects---complete at moderate bias ($d \to 0$ at $n = 355$), ${>}60\%$ attenuation at stronger effects---confirmed by seven statistical methods.
6	Whether this reflects measurement attenuation or construct divergence, Likert-only audits miss style-driven preferences that propagate through alignment pipelines.
7	Second, GEE conditional decomposition demonstrates per-axis confound structure consistent across four target architectures---verbosity style-dominated, formality conditional, register judge-dependent---determining which estimates require conditional analysis and informing debiasing priorities.
8	
9	Pairwise comparison offers superior detection sensitivity for style bias, provided that amplification controls are in place (\S\ref{sec:amplification}); existing Likert-based null findings may reflect measurement insensitivity rather than genuine absence of bias.
